headline: Full AI Content Pipeline Built for iGaming using n8n, Gemini, Claude, and Vertex AI
summary: This advanced system automates content ingestion, generation, translation, and quality checks for iGaming platforms, ensuring legal compliance and scalability across thousands of game listings and reviews.
details: Running an online casino platform requires keeping thousands of game listings, multilingual descriptions, and structured reviews fresh, a task that doesn't scale manually. This project details a full production line built using n8n, orchestrated across Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and Vertex AI RAG.

The pipeline ingests content from casino sites and source documents, processes it through n8n, and passes it to Gemini, Claude, and Vertex AI for generation. Content is stored in Cloud Storage and the Vertex RAG index, then assembled, translated, quality-checked, and published into a Payload CMS running on Next.js.

The data ingestion layer uses Scrapfly to fetch server-side rendered pages from JavaScript-heavy casino sites, converting the HTML to clean Markdown. This aggregated content is then written to Google Cloud Storage, ready for vectorization and indexing in Vertex AI Search.

The RAG engine is a technically interesting piece, handling all interactions with Vertex AI's RAG corpus for fetching, filtering, and semantic searching. It's crucial for ensuring the pipeline generates trustworthy and accurate content, rather than just generic copy.

The corpus contains both operator facts like bonus terms and game catalogues, as well as per-country legal and regulatory rules. This dual truth makes the engine genuinely valuable in regulated markets, ensuring generated reviews comply with local laws without manual editor checks.

The core review pipeline is the system's centerpiece, combining RAG retrieval, structured outline generation, and section-by-section writing. This workflow brings together all previously built components to produce a finished, publish-ready casino review.

headline_marked: [[macOS computer use 1.8x faster, 85% cheaper]] than cua-driver alone with new MCP server
headline: macOS computer use 1.8x faster, 85% cheaper than cua-driver alone with new MCP server
summary: A new server built on cua-driver and beans-picker allows Claude Code to operate macOS apps in the background, drastically cutting down task time and token costs.
details: A new MCP server, dubbed beans-picker, significantly boosts the efficiency of macOS automation using Claude Code. Benchmark tasks ran 1.8 times faster and cost 85% less than using cua-driver alone, with median times dropping from 49.7s to 28.1s and costs from $0.388 to $0.060.

The core innovation lies in reducing the amount of data sent to the AI model. Traditional methods with cua-driver involve sending the entire window accessibility tree and a screenshot at each step, leading to high token usage and longer processing times.

The original cua-driver is effective for background macOS interaction but becomes expensive when an AI agent repeatedly requests full UI context. A typical five-step task required five or more full reads, consuming around 646,000 Claude tokens.

The beans-picker server replaces these extensive reads with a short list of candidate actions and a summary of changes. This dramatically reduces the token count, as the model only receives relevant, actionable information instead of the full UI tree.

The server provides three tools: `observe` for listing candidates, `act` for performing actions and checking results, and `extract` for reading values. This allows the AI agent to make precise decisions with minimal input.

To implement this setup, users need macOS, Python 3.12+, cua-driver with necessary permissions, a Jev API key, and Xcode Command Line Tools. Specific accessibility settings must also be enabled for beans-picker.

Privacy is maintained as window text only leaves the machine when a step explicitly requires Jev. The project is a personal hobby and is not affiliated with Cua/trycua or TypeSafe, with cua-driver and Jev being separate components.
